newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Pol Pot mystery to linger in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Pol Pot mystery to linger in Cambodia.

text.p: Even as his enemies close in around him, few are confident Pol Pot will be taken alive to stand trial for crimes against humanity.
As with Adolf Hitler, the true fate of Cambodia's notorious leader probably will never be known, some analysts say.

A charred corpse was all that appeared to remain of Hitler, Nazi Germany's leader, after Russian armies closed in on Berlin in 1945. Identity was never fully established and speculation persists over whether his death was real or faked.
Cambodian authorities have said they hope Pol Pot will be captured and led back to Phnom Penh in chains. Others believe his end, like much of his life, will be shrouded in mystery.
Some suggested a death could be faked, allowing Pol Pot to disappear while less-despised members of his Khmer Rouge emerge from the jungle to join mainstream politics.

"The government won't produce a body. I think the line we will be fed is that he died on a stretcher of inadequate medical treatment, he was positively identified and buried by his bodyguards," said one military analyst.

He said there was a reason for "duping people" -- Pol Pot's reported death could make more palatable First Prime Minister Norodom Ranariddh's planned alliance with Pol Pot aide Khieu Samphan or other guerrillas.
"They have this story to allow Khieu Samphan into politics... they know he's always been the acceptable face of the Khmer Rouge," a foreign analyst said.
Such a result might be useful in domestic political terms but would leave many human rights activists in Cambodia and elsewhere dissatisfied.

Between one and three million people died from starvation, execution, disease and hard labour in the killing fields of Cambodia during Pol Pot's disastrous experiment with total communism between 1975 and 1979.

As Cambodia's population at the time was only six million, his accusers say the slaughter placed Pol Pot near the top of history's league of mass murderers. Pol Pot last appeared in public 18 years ago, shortly after a Vietnamese invasion overthrew his regime. He said then that several thousand Cambodians had died from "some mistakes" in implementing his policies and denied committing crimes against humanity.
Then he disappeared into the north jungles.
He is now almost 70 years old now and believed to be suffering from malaria. There have also been reports in the past of his death.
Most analysts say the true condition and fate of Pol Pot probably will remain as impenetrable as the jungle he has hidden in for almost two decades.
"We'll know for sure in a couple of days that we'll never know," predicted the military analyst.
